THESE PETITIONS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.
These five separate petitions are filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners.
2. Petitioner-Gururaj is the husband of Smt.Gracemary who is the complainant.

Petitioner- Channavva Kusugal is the mother, petitioner-Muttanna @ Channabasappa Kusugal and Sangamesh Gururaj Gurusiddappa Kusugal vs Smt Gracemary W/O Gururaj Kusugal on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45522818/

sentences.text: Petitioner-Ashwini Gatti and Shakuntala Gatti are the cousins of Gururaj.

3. At the instance of Gracemary, criminal proceedings are initiated in C.C.No.334/2020 for the offences punishable u/sections 498A, 504, 506 r/w/s 34 Indian Penal Code on the file of JMFC II,
Belagavi against four persons, but charge sheet is filed against only Gururaj and Ashwini.
Challenging the same, Ashwini Gatti filed criminal proceedings in Crl.P.No.101495/2020 which came to be allowed and criminal proceedings against her were quashed.
5. Gururaj Kusugal has filed Crl.P.No.100815/2023.

6. Gracemary has also filed Crl.Misc.No.18/2022 u/s 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (for short, 'the D.V.Act') against all the petitioners herein and Smt.Parvati who died during the pendency of the proceedings.

sentences.text: 7. Challenging the proceeding under the D.V.Act, Ashwini Gatti and Shakuntala Gatti have filed Crl.P.No.100859/2022.
Muttanna alias Channabasappa Kusugal, Sangamesh @ Sangappa Kusugal and Channavva Kusugal have filed Crl.P.No.100376/2022.
Gururaj Kusugal has filed Crl.P.No.100816/2023.

Now a compromise petition is filed duly signed by the complainant-Gracemary and Gururaj Kusugal, by which they have settled their dispute in the following terms:
"4.
At the intervention of elders and well - wishers of all the parties, have agreed for the settlement of all the above said litigations pending between all the parties.
It Is submitted that ultimately the litigations were because of marital relationship between Gururaj S/o Gurusiddappa Kusugal and Smt. Gracemary W/o. Gururaj Kusugal.

Therefore, it is agreed between the Gururaj and Gracemary as follows:-
i) Gururaj has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.
11,00,000/(one time settlement) towards full and final settlement of all the above said litigations as well as for dissolution of marriage.
As Gururaj has already deposited Rs.3,00,000/- before the JMFC II, Belgaum, Gururaj has no objection to get the said amount released by Smt. Gracemary w/o. Gururaj Kusugal.
In so far as remaining amount of 8,00,000/- is concerned the same is paid by way of DD No. 451268 dated 17.04.2023 for Rs.7,00,000/- cash.
Copy of the DD is produced herewith for the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court.

sentences.text: At this stage, it is relevant to refer to some of the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court with regard to the directions and guidelines issued for accepting or rejecting the settlement between the parties.

10. In the case of Narindra Singh V/s. State of Punjab1 (Narindra Singh's case), at paragraph 31, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down principles by which the High Court would be guided in giving Gururaj Gurusiddappa Kusugal vs Smt Gracemary W/O Gururaj Kusugal on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45522818/

10.1. In Gian Singh V/s. State of Punjab and another2, (Gian Singh's Case), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has discussed the scope of the power of trial Court 2014 AIR SCW 2065 (2012) 10 SCC 303 - 12 - C/W CRL.P No. 100376 of 2022, CRL.P No. 100815 of 2023, CRL.P No. 100816 of 2023, in excising the discretion under Section 320 of Cr.P.C and that of the High Court exercising inherited powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Yogendra Yadav Vs. State of Jharkhand and another3, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the High Court can quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., even though the offence alleged is non- compoundable, if parties have amicably settled their disputes and victim has no objection.

entities.text: Yogendra Yadav Vs. State of Jharkhand and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, this would depend on the facts of each case.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court also held that offences which involve moral turpitude, grave offences like rape, murder cannot be effaced by quashing proceedings because they have harmful effect on Society and are not restricted to individuals or groups.
Quashing of such offence may send a wrong signal to the Society.

However, if the High Court is convinced that the offences are individual or personal in nature and not affecting the public peace or tranquility and (2014) 9 SCC 653 - 13 - C/W CRL.P No. 100376 of 2022, CRL.P No. 100815 of 2023, CRL.P No. 100816 of 2023, quashing of proceedings on account of compromise would secure the ends of justice, it may quash the same.
In such case, the prosecution becomes lame and pursuing such lame prosecution may become waste of time and energy and also unsettle compromise and obstruct restoration of peace.
11. In the light of the above decisions, it would be necessary to examine whether this is a fit case to accept the compromise between the parties.
12. The parties to the proceedings i.e., respondent No.2-complainant-Gracemary is the wife of petitioner Gururaj.
The other petitioners are related to Gururaj.
It appears on account of matrimonial discord between the respondent-complainant and petitioner-Gururaj, criminal complaint and proceedings under D.V.Act are initiated.
The remaining petitioners are also roped in.
petitioner-Gururaj and respondent-complainant-Gracemary have also agreed to get their marriage dissolved.

In the light of these - 14 - C/W CRL.P No. 100376 of 2022, CRL.P No. 100815 of 2023, CRL.P No. 100816 of 2023,
developments, it is in the interest of the parties to accept the settlement between them.

Taking into consideration these aspects, this Court is of the considered opinion that these are fit cases to accept the compromise.

In the light of the compromise entered into between the parties, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The petitions are disposed of in terms of the compromise and further proceedings in C.C.No.334/2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A,
504, 506 r/w/s 34 Indian Penal Code on the file of JMFC II, Belagavi and Crl.Misc.18/2020 u/s 12 of the D.V.Act on the file of JMFC II, Belagavi are quashed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
adequate treatment to the settlement between the parties and exercising its power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C while accepting the settlement and quashing the proceedings or refusing to accept the settlement with a direction to continue with the criminal proceedings.
In Yogendra Yadav Vs. State of Jharkhand and another3, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the High Court can quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., even though the offence alleged is non- compoundable, if parties have amicably settled their disputes and victim has no objection.
Quashing of such offence may send a wrong signal to the Society.
However, if the High Court is convinced that the offences are individual or personal in nature and not affecting the public peace or tranquility and (2014) 9 SCC 653 - 13 - C/W CRL.P No. 100376 of 2022, CRL.P No. 100815 of 2023, CRL.P No. 100816 of 2023, quashing of proceedings on account of compromise would secure the ends of justice, it may quash the same.
In such case, the prosecution becomes lame and pursuing such lame prosecution may become waste of time and energy and also unsettle compromise and obstruct restoration of peace.
12. The parties to the proceedings i.e., respondent No.2-complainant-Gracemary is the wife of petitioner Gururaj.
It appears on account of matrimonial discord between the respondent-complainant and petitioner-Gururaj, criminal complaint and proceedings under D.V.Act are initiated.
the offences alleged are not of such nature so as to affect the society at large.
